path.description: Path to the source file containing the symbol (absolute or relative to project root)

symbol.description: Name of the symbol to analyze

depth.description: Max traversal depth (default: call_tree=5, callers=1, trace_to=10, trace_to_symbol=10 capped at 16, impact=5, trace_data=5)

expression.description: Expression to track through data flow (required for trace_data op)

toSymbol.description: Target symbol name for trace_to_symbol; the returned path ends at this symbol

toPath.description: Optional target file for trace_to_symbol; required when toSymbol exists in multiple files

includeTests.description: Include test files in callers/paths. Defaults to false; tests are hidden.

includeUnresolved.description: Show every unresolved external/stdlib call individually. Defaults to false; unresolved leaf calls are collapsed into one summary per parent.

path.description: Optional path inside the git repository or worktree to inspect (absolute or relative to project root). Conflicts are discovered from that repository's top level. Defaults to the session project root.

files.description: Paths to delete (one or more). May include directories when recursive=true.

recursive.description: Required to delete a directory and its contents. Defaults to false; passing a directory without this returns an error.

path.description: Path to the file (absolute or relative to project root)

module.description: Module path (required for add, remove — e.g. 'react', './utils', 'std::fmt')

names.description: Named imports to add. Each entry uses the language's native named-import text, including per-name aliasing where the language uses `as` (e.g. ['useState', 'debounce as db'], Solidity ['ERC20', 'IERC20 as IToken']).

namespace.description: Namespace binding: `import * as ns from 'mod'` (ES), `import * as N from "./X.sol"` (Solidity).

alias.description: Whole-module alias. Solidity: `import "./X.sol" as X` (module=path, alias=X).

modifiers.description: Statement-level modifier tokens, language-validated: Java/C# 'static'; C# 'global'/'unsafe'; Java/Kotlin/Scala 'wildcard'; Swift '@testable'. Unsupported tokens for the file's language return a clear error.

removeName.description: Named import to remove for 'remove' op; omit to remove entire import

validate.description: Validation level: 'syntax' (default) or 'full'. Syntax = tree-sitter parse check only. Full = also runs LSP type-checking (slower, catches more errors)

sections.description: Categories to include in detailed drill-down (e.g. 'todos' or ['todos', 'dead_code', 'cycles']). Use 'all' for every active category. Omit for summary-only mode. With scope, listing sections without 'diagnostics' (or 'all') skips diagnostics work; omitting sections keeps diagnostics. Other categories are verified regardless of sections.

scope.description: Restrict returned results to paths under this scope (one path, or an array of paths — not a space-separated list; file or directory; absolute or relative to project root). `scope=` narrows results. Scoped requests collect diagnostics for the scoped files and report coverage gaps, unless sections lists other categories and leaves out 'diagnostics'.

offset.description: Rows to skip independently in each drill-down list. Default 0; follow next_offset in each list envelope.

topK.description: Max drill-down items per category. Default 20, max 100.

path.description: Source file path to move (absolute or relative to project root)

destination.description: Destination file path (absolute or relative to project root)

target.description: What to outline: a file path, directory path, URL, or array of paths. The mode is auto-detected: URLs by `http://`/`https://` prefix, directories by stat, arrays as multi-file.

files.description: Directory-only mode: when true, target must be a directory or array of directories and the result is a breadth-first file tree with directory rollups plus language, symbol, and line counts.

includeTests.description: Directory outline only: include test files. Defaults to false; tests are hidden.

path.description: File path (required for history, optional for undo, optional for checkpoint — snapshots only that file when files is omitted, optional for restore — restores only that file, required for purge — a file or directory). Absolute or relative to project root

files.description: Specific files to include in checkpoint, or to restore from a checkpoint (optional; restore without path/files restores the whole checkpoint; explicit checkpoint files may be untracked or gitignored)

query.description: Concept, regex, literal text, filename, or capability to find. Examples: 'fuzzy match with whitespace tolerance', '^export', 'Cargo.lock'. Optional when `pattern` is given.

pattern.description: Regex (grep syntax, case-sensitive) for names or text that must appear, e.g. 'load_config|ConfigLoader'. Ranked with `query` when both are given.

includeTests.description: Include test files (*.test.*, *_test.rs, __tests__/, …) plus test-support, fixture, mock, snapshot, and corpus files. Defaults to false.

path.description: Only set this to search a different project or plain folder (absolute or ~ path). Omit it for the current configured workspace, including non-Git workspace roots; this is not a subdirectory filter. Unindexed external folders use a bounded lexical fallback; filesystem roots, home and its ancestors are refused.

batch.description: One or more lookups; entries may mix file paths and URLs

target.description: File path (absolute or project-relative) or HTTP/HTTPS URL, auto-detected; issue://N or pr://N when GitHub reads are enabled

symbols.description: Symbol name for code or heading text for Markdown/HTML; a string or array of strings

contextLines.description: Lines of context before/after each symbol (default: 3)

callgraph.description: Include call-graph annotations for every entry (default: false)

pattern.description: AST pattern with meta-variables ($VAR, $$$). Must be complete AST node.
AST pattern with meta-variables ($VAR, $$$). Must be complete AST node.

contextLines.description: Number of context lines to show around each match

taskId.description: Background task ID returned by shell({ background: true }), e.g. bash-6b454047a1c39ded.
Background task ID returned by shell({ background: true }), e.g. bash-6b454047a1c39ded.

outputOffset.description: Read a bounded stdout/PTY byte page from this offset; returns masked text and the next byte offset.

stderrOffset.description: Read a bounded stderr byte page from this offset; returns masked text and the next byte offset.

outputMode.description: PTY output rendering mode. Defaults to screen for PTY tasks and preserves existing behavior for piped tasks when omitted.

taskId.description: Background task ID returned by shell({ background: true }).

pattern.description: Substring or regex pattern. Optional in sync mode; required with background:true. Sync substring watches keep only the overlap tail needed for boundary matches; sync regex watches use a 64 KB rolling output window.

background.description: When true, register an async watch and return immediately. Defaults to false (sync wait).

timeoutMs.description: Sync-only timeout in milliseconds. In a main session: default 30000, max `bash.watch_sync_max_ms` (120000 by default). In a delegated session: omit it to wait up to the worker wait limit (`bash.worker_wait_max_ms`, 30 minutes by default), after which the watch reports the command is still running; a value you pass is clamped to that worker limit.

deliver.description: Async-only: batch every matching complete line, fold consecutive duplicates, and report cap drops with byte offsets.

once.description: Async-only. Defaults true; false keeps the watch sticky until task exit.

taskId.description: Background PTY task ID returned by shell({ pty: true, background: true }).

input.description: Either a string of verbatim bytes (e.g. 'print(1)\n') OR an array mixing strings and { key: '<name>' } objects for atomic text+key sequences. Example: [ 'iHello', { key: 'esc' }, ':wq', { key: 'enter' } ].

path.description: Path to the file to edit (absolute or relative to project root)

symbol.description: Named symbol to replace; only meaningful together with `content`. A call carrying one without the other is incomplete.

content.description: Replacement content for symbol mode; only meaningful together with `symbol`. A call carrying one without the other is incomplete. For whole-file writes, use the `write` tool.

appendContent.description: Text to append to the end of path; creates the file if needed

edits.description: Batch edits — non-empty array of { oldString, newString }, { oldString, newString, replaceAll: true }, or { startLine, endLine, content } objects

oldString.description: Text to find for a batch find/replace edit

newString.description: Replacement text for a batch find/replace edit

replaceAll.description: Replace every occurrence for this batch item

occurrence.description: 1-based occurrence for this batch item (1 = first match)

startLine.description: 1-based start line for a batch line-range edit

endLine.description: 1-based end line for a batch line-range edit

content.description: Replacement text for a batch line-range edit

offset.description: Rows of shown results to skip; follow the next offset the reply names.

path.description: Path to file or directory (absolute or relative to project root)

startLine.description: 1-based line or directory entry to start reading from

endLine.description: 1-based line or directory entry to stop reading at (inclusive)

limit.description: Max lines (default: 2000) or directory entries (default and cap: 1000) to return

offset.description: 1-based line or directory entry to start reading from (use with limit). Ignored if startLine is provided

command.description: Shell command to execute. Supports pipes, redirection, and normal shell syntax.

timeout.description: Hard kill cap in milliseconds (positive integer). In the default foreground mode when wait is false, a command that exceeds the configured wait window is promoted to background and gets a completion reminder when it exits; wait:true disables promotion and remains inline until completion, timeout, or bash.worker_wait_max_ms. A background task with no timeout is killed after 30 minutes; pass a longer timeout for long jobs.

workdir.description: Working directory for command execution. Relative paths resolve through the bridge; defaults to the current tool context/project root when omitted.

description.description: Short 5-10 word human-readable summary shown in OpenCode UI metadata instead of raw shell syntax.

wait.description: When true, run in the foreground without auto-promoting and wait until the command finishes or reaches its timeout (at most bash.worker_wait_max_ms, 30 minutes by default; the command then keeps running in the background and the reply says how to keep waiting); Any new message detaches this wait. Set `bash.detach_on_user_message: false` to keep it blocking; even then, a message containing the literal `&detach` forces detachment, and the token is stripped before delivery and the rest of the message is preserved; a token-only message becomes `(requested background detach)`. Use only when you know the result is required before doing anything else.

background.description: When true, spawn the command in the background and return a taskId for bash_status/bash_kill instead of waiting for completion. Defaults to false. A background task with no timeout is killed after 30 minutes; pass a longer timeout for long jobs.

compressed.description: When true or omitted, return compressed output with noisy terminal control sequences reduced. Set to false for raw output.

pty.description: When true, spawn the command in a real PTY for interactive programs (python/node/bash REPLs, vim). Implies background: true automatically. Inspect with bash_status({ taskId, outputMode: "screen" }) and drive interactively with bash_write — its input accepts either a string OR an array like [ "iHello", { key: "esc" }, ":wq", { key: "enter" } ] for atomic text+key sequences.

ptyRows.description: PTY terminal height in rows — ignored when pty is false. Defaults to 24 when pty: true. Minimum 1, maximum 60.

ptyCols.description: PTY terminal width in columns — ignored when pty is false. Defaults to 80 when pty: true. Minimum 1, maximum 140.

id.description: The ID of an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

description.description: A short 3-5 word label for the task, displayed to the user

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. It must be a chat model; image and decision models can't run subagents. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look the model up with the models tool, filtering to your own provider first.

sessionID.description: Send a follow-up to an existing subagent, running or finished. Omit to start a new one.

background.description: Run the subagent in the background and return immediately. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress.

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in. Defaults to markdown.

path.description: Path to the file to write (absolute or relative to project root)

content.description: The full content to write to the file; for issue://N / pr://N, the comment body to post
